summary: Platte Mountain lookout, Butte County, Cal Fire: CCC-built tower moved from Lone Pine in 1956 (NHLR; 1955 per Peakbagging). Standing in 2017 photo; NHLR-registered 2019.

facts.design: Tower about 92 to 93 feet tall with a 7-foot square cab and catwalk; NHLR says 92 ft, Peakbagging says 93 ft
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire)

events.note: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register: the Lone Pine lookout was constructed as early as 1920. Not confirmed as the same tower the NHLR calls CCC-built, and no source read gives the CCC build year
NHLR: a lookout stood at Lone Pine as early as 1924. Not reconciled with the 1920 record
NHLR: CDF moved the CCC-built Lone Pine tower and house to Platte Mountain in 1956; the tower was extended to 92 ft and the cab remodeled for a catwalk in the same entry. Peakbagging gives 1955
CAL FIRE June 2008 list names the Platt Mountain Lookout among lookouts that may be staffed during the 2008 fire season

corrections.proposed: Built by the CCC at Lone Pine (build year not given in sources read); relocated to Platte Mountain in 1956
corrections.why: NHLR gives 1956 as the year CDF moved the CCC-built tower to its present site, not the year it was built

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1956; the Peakbagging photo page gives 1955. The event uses 1956 from the NHLR and the story reports both.
NHLR says a lookout stood there as early as 1924; the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register says constructed as early as 1920. Not reconciled.
NHLR says the tower and house moved to Platte Mountain; the Former Fire Lookout Sites page says the Lone Pine cabin may have gone to Pratt Mountain. Not reconciled.
NHLR gives 3,473 ft (1,059 m); Peakbagging gives 3540 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.
NHLR gives 92 ft; Peakbagging gives 93 ft. height_m uses 92 ft.
CAL FIRE's 2008 list spells it Platt Mountain Lookout; NHLR and Peakbagging use Platte.

notes_for_editor: No source read says whether the public may visit or climb the tower, so no access level is recorded. The CCC build year is not in any source read. Sources disagree on the 1955/1956 move and the Lone Pine start date (1920 vs 1924). The Weebly page for Platte is only a county index and is not cited. The 2008 CAL FIRE list is the only staffing source besides the 2017 photo page. The first record's 1956 build date is a relocation date.
